records.content_text:
A factor is any of the two or more whole numbers we multiply to get a product. For example: $6 \times 2 = 12$. The numbers 6 and 2 are factors of 12.

A factor is also described as a whole number that divides into a larger number without a remainder. For example: $\frac{12}{6} = 2$. The number 6 divides perfectly into 12. Therefore, the number 6 is a factor of 12.

placement.rationale: This worked example finds all factors of a whole number.

records.evidence_quote: Find all the factors of the number 60.
records.prompt_text: Find all the factors of the number 60.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Any number larger than 1 has the number itself and 1 as factors.

$$
1 \times 60=60
$$

Step 2: Start with 2 and see if it divides into 60 without a remainder.

$$
\frac{60}{2} = 30
$$

$$
2 \times 30=60
$$

Step 3: Try each consecutive number to see if it divides into 60 without a remainder. Stop when you get to a number that you already have as an answer.

$$
\begin{array}{2}
 \frac{60}{3} = 20 \hspace{10mm} &3 \times 20 = 60 \\
 \frac{60}{4} = 15 &4 \times 15 = 60 \\
 \frac{60}{5} = 12 &5 \times 12 = 60 \\
 \frac{60}{6} = 10 &6 \times 10 = 60 \\
 \end{array}
$$

The numbers 7, 8 and 9 do not divide into 60 without a remainder, so they are not factors of 60.

You already have the number 10, as 60 divided by 6 is 10, so you can stop there.

$$
\frac{60}{10} = 6
$$

Step 4: List all the factors from the smallest number to the largest number.

The factors of 60 are: 1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6; 10; 12; 15; 20; 30; 60

heading_path.h1: Chapter 2: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple

placement.rationale: This worked example expresses 80 as a product of prime factors.

records.evidence_quote: Find the prime factors of 80.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Find the smallest prime number that is a factor of 80. Express 80 as a product of two factors.

$$
\frac{80}{2}=40
$$

$$
80=2 \times 40
$$

Step 2: Find the smallest prime number that is a factor of the non-prime factor from Step 1. Express 80 as a product of three factors.

$$
\frac{40}{2}=20
$$

$$
80=2 \times 2 \times 20
$$

Step 3: Repeat Step 2 until 80 is expressed as a product of only prime numbers.

$$
\frac{20}{2}=10
$$

$$
80=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 10
$$

$$
\frac{10}{2}=5
$$

$$
80=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5
$$

Remember that 1 is not a prime number.

records.content_text: Finding and writing down the prime factors of large numbers can become confusing. To make the process easier, we may use continued division and write the prime factors in index form. The index or power of a number tells us how many times we multiply the number by itself. For example, $2^4$ means $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$. In this case, 4 is the power or index of 2.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 2.3: Prime factors in index form

placement.issue: The worked example writes prime factors in index form.
placement.rationale: The worked example practices the candidate index-form objective.

records.evidence_quote: Find the prime factors of 180 and write them in index form.
records.prompt_text: Find the prime factors of 180 and write them in index form.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Divide the smallest prime factor of 180 until it cannot divide any further.

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 180  ewline
 \hline
 2 & 90  ewline
 \hline
 & 45
\end{array}
$$

Step 2: Move to the next prime factor of 180. Keep on dividing until it cannot divide any further.

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 180  ewline
 \hline
 2 & 90  ewline
 \hline
 3 & 45  ewline
 \hline
 3 & 15  ewline
 \hline
 & 5
\end{array}
$$

Step 3: Repeat Step 2 until you get 1 as an answer.

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 180  ewline
 \hline
 2 & 90  ewline
 \hline
 3 & 45  ewline
 \hline
 3 & 15  ewline
 \hline
 5 & 5  ewline
 \hline
 & 1
\end{array}
$$

Step 4: Write down all the prime factors of 180. Use superscripts to write the index of each prime factor, that is, how many times the prime factor divided.

$$
180 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5
$$

The index of each prime factor shows us how many times we must multiply each prime factor to get 180 again:

$$
180 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5
$$
